### Description

On CUDA, replaces `csrc/fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` with a CuTe DSL module, `vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, per @tlrmchlsmth's request on #63308 (closed): no DSv4-only kernel object code in the wheel, no extension compile time.

Same four entry points, same positional schemas, so call sites keep their argument lists. Math is ported bit for bit: fp32 accumulation, bf16 double-round before the absmax, warp shuffle reduction order, UE8M0 exponent-field scales, both paged record layouts (V4 584 B/token, V4.1 mxfp8 528 B/token), the full-cache bf16/fp8 variants, and graph-replay-safe launches. Scalar min/max/abs/rsqrt use the DSL's `cute.arch`/`cute.math` ops rather than hand-rolled helpers, and compile to the same instructions the .cu's intrinsics compiled to, with NaN handling following the hardware ops as in the .cu.

**ROCm is preserved.** The `.cu` stays but is built only for HIP (`CMakeLists.txt`), with its four torch ops registered under `#ifdef USE_ROCM`, so CUDA builds no longer compile or ship the kernel and AMD behavior is unchanged. The six production call sites (deepseek_v4/v41 attention and dspark) import the four functions from a new dispatch module, `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_dispatch`, which routes ROCm to the extension op and everything else to the CuTe DSL module (imported lazily, failing closed with a named RuntimeError when nvidia-cutlass-dsl is missing).

The `kv`-only entry point also takes optional `kv_norm_weight`/`kv_norm_eps`; current call sites leave them unset, and the ROCm op does not take them (the dispatch raises `NotImplementedError` there instead).

### Performance vs the preserved .cu (H200)

Benchmarks ran on an H200 (sm_90a, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0). The `.cu` is JIT-compiled with the CMake flags this file builds with (`-O3`, no fast-math, sm_90). Inputs are identical for both implementations, and timing uses CUDA-graph replay so the numbers are kernel-only. The benchmark checks correctness on every case (`q_max_ulp`, `q_bits_differ`, `k_bytes_differ`).

Measurements on the initial port (`a3f899ebab`):

| op (kernel-only µs) | `.cu` | DSL | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| quant_insert, 8192 tok | 447 | 1070 | DSL 2.4× slower |
| quant_insert, 2048 tok | 118 | 291 | DSL 2.5× slower |
| quant_insert, 512 tok | 41 | 88 | DSL 2.1× slower |
| quant_insert, decode (1 tok) | 2.4 | 3.0 | DSL 25% slower |
| kv_rope_insert | 6.6 | 6.8 | equal |
| full_cache_fp8 | 41 | 39 | equal |
| full_cache_bf16 | 44 | 82 | DSL 1.8× slower |

At 8192 tokens the `.cu` moves ~1.6 GB (536 MB live-Q read + 1.07 GB padded-Q write) in 447 µs ≈ 3.6 TB/s, near the practical HBM3e ceiling (4.8 TB/s peak). The initial DSL port reached ~1.4 TB/s.

Measurements on this branch (`901bb03375`):

| op (kernel-only µs) | `.cu` kernel | `.cu` | DSL | DSL speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| quant_insert, 8192 tok | `fusedDeepseekV4QNormRopeKVRopeQuantInsertKernelReducedGrid` | 450 | 396 | 1.14× |
| quant_insert, 2048 tok | `fusedDeepseekV4QNormRopeKVRopeQuantInsertKernelReducedGrid` | 118 | 101 | 1.17× |
| quant_insert, 512 tok | `fusedDeepseekV4QNormRopeKVRopeQuantInsertKernel` | 41 | 27 | 1.51× |
| quant_insert, 64 tok | `fusedDeepseekV4QNormRopeKVRopeQuantInsertKernel` | 7.4 | 4.5 | 1.64× |
| quant_insert, decode (1 tok) | `fusedDeepseekV4QNormRopeKVRopeQuantInsertKernel` | 2.4 | 2.0 | 1.20× |
| kv_rope_insert, 8192 tok | `fusedDeepseekV4QNormRopeKVRopeQuantInsertKernel`, zero query heads | 6.6 | 5.8 | 1.15× |
| full_cache_bf16, 4096 tok | `fusedDeepseekV4FullCacheKernel` | 47.4 | 37.2 | 1.28× |
| full_cache_bf16, 2048/1024/512/256/128 tok | `fusedDeepseekV4FullCacheKernel` | 17.2/9.1/5.7/3.9/2.9 | 15.2/8.6/5.6/3.5/2.3 | 1.13× / 1.06× / 1.03× / 1.11× / 1.24× |
| full_cache_fp8, 4096/512/128 tok | `fusedDeepseekV4FullCacheKernel` | 40.0/5.1/2.8 | 29.6/4.5/2.4 | 1.35× / 1.11× / 1.15× |

Every case is faster. The closest is full_cache_bf16 T=512 (5.72 vs 5.55 µs), whose 68 MB working set is L2-resident and latency-bound for both implementations. The `.cu` launcher still switches to its reduced-grid kernel at 1024 tokens (`NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF`); the DSL module no longer has a reduced-grid variant (see the launch-geometry section below). kv_rope_insert with a packed uint8 cache schedules the quant-insert kernel with zero query heads, and both full-cache dtypes run `fusedDeepseekV4FullCacheKernel`. quant_insert outputs are bit-exact against the `.cu` at every size (zero differing bits, zero differing cache bytes). Over runs on the final artifact, T=2048 measured `.cu` 118.5–118.7 µs vs DSL 101.0–101.1 µs, and T=8192 measured `.cu` 448.4–450.0 µs vs DSL 396.0–396.3 µs.

Each fix below came from diffing the DSL-generated SASS against the `.cu` SASS.

#### 128-bit vectorized memory access (`668d0b3bbd`)

The initial port touched memory through per-element DSL tensor indexing, which lowered to 32-bit loads and stores. Reworking the layouts so each lane's 16 elements move as one folded `cute.copy` with a 128-bit copy atom gave the paged kernel LDG.128/STG.128 and took quant_insert T=8192 from 1070 to ~453 µs (~1.4 to ~3.5 TB/s). The kernel is bandwidth-limited after this change, matching the `.cu`.

#### bf16 encode/store tail as one inline-asm block (`668d0b3bbd`)

This change fixed full_cache_bf16 (T=4096: 82 → 37.8 µs). The full-cache Q path ends with eight `cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32` (F2FP) feeding two 128-bit stores. In the DSL-generated SASS the eight conversions issued back-to-back and both stores waited on the last F2FP with nothing left to overlap. The `.cu` does not have this tail because its store address comes from runtime division and modulo, a long integer dependency chain that interleaves with the conversions.

The fix is `_q_tail_store_bf16`, a single inline-asm PTX block that owns both the conversions and the address math, hand-interleaved so the two chains hide each other:

```ptx
{
    .reg .b32 t0, t1, w0..w7;  .reg .b64 d0, d1;
    shl.b32            t0, $3, 8;               // slot   -> word offset
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w0, $6, $5;
    cvt.u64.u32        d0, t0;
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w1, $8, $7;
    mad.wide.u32       d1, $2, {row_words}, d0;  // token*row_words + slot
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w2, $10, $9;
    shl.b32            t1, $4, 3;                // lane   -> word offset
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w3, $12, $11;
    cvt.u64.u32        d0, t1;
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w4, $14, $13;
    add.u64            d1, d1, d0;
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w5, $16, $15;
    shl.b64            d1, d1, 2;                // words  -> bytes
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w6, $18, $17;
    add.u64            d1, d1, $1;               // + tensor base
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w7, $20, $19;
    st.global.v4.b32   [d1],    {w0, w1, w2, w3};
    st.global.v4.b32   [d1+16], {w4, w5, w6, w7};
}
```

The tensor base comes from `q.iterator.to_llvm_ptr()` → `llvm.ptrtoint(T.i64())` and is bound with the `l` constraint. `row_words` is a per-compile-key constant (`HQ * 256`), baked into the asm string as an immediate rather than passed as a register operand. The block is marked `has_side_effects=True` for the stores. It is bit-exact against `cute.copy` + `_encode_words` on every suite case, because the DSL's `fp32x2_to_bf16x2` lowers to `cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32`.

The asm tail slows the paged kernel at large T. Routing the paged kernel's Q store through this block (measured, then rejected) took T=2048 from 120.3 to 126.4 µs (0.94×) and T=8192 from 452.8 to 469.9 µs (0.96×). At 3.5+ TB/s, issuing stores early matters more than hiding conversion latency, and `cute.copy`'s folded store address issues earlier than an address chain interleaved with the conversions. The paged kernel keeps `cute.copy`, and only the latency-bound full-cache kernel uses the asm tail.

#### Rope-lane-guarded cos/sin loads in the paged kernels (`3f5bb3ad31`)

This change closed the last sub-parity cases (quant_insert T=2048/8192, 0.98×/0.99× → 1.09×/1.10×). RoPE only touches the last `ROPE_DIM` of each 512-dim head, which is 4 of 32 lanes per warp (`dim_base >= NOPE_DIM`). The rope step in the DSL was already guarded by that condition, but the cos/sin loads were not. SASS of the paged kernel before the fix contains four unpredicated `LDG.E.128` per lane on all 32 lanes:

```
/*1ca0*/  LDG.E.128 R8,  desc[UR6][R28.64+0x80] ;
/*1cb0*/  LDG.128   R12, desc[UR6][R28.64] ;
/*1cc0*/  LDG.E.128 R16, desc[UR6][R28.64+0x90] ;
/*1cd0*/  LDG.E.128 R20, desc[UR6][R28.64+0x10] ;
```

That is 2 KB of L2-resident loads per warp per slot where 256 B suffice. `_load_cos_sin` also computes `half_base = (dim_base - NOPE_DIM) >> 1`, which is negative on the 28 non-rope lanes, so those lanes loaded from out-of-bounds addresses (the values were never consumed, which is why nothing failed). The `.cu` guards all of this behind `is_rope_lane`. Guarding the `pos_ids` fetch and `_load_cos_sin` call with the same `dim_base >= NOPE_DIM` condition the rope step already uses is semantically identical (`pos` and `cos_v`/`sin_v` have no other reader) and improved T=2048/8192 by ~10% and mid T by 4-8% (T=64 1.39×→1.55×, T=512 1.44×→1.50×), at a small cost in the decode-size case (T=1 1.32×→1.21×).

The same guard slows the full-cache kernel. Applying it to the full-cache kernel's two identical load sites (measured, then reverted) dropped T=128 from 1.19× to 1.04×, T=256 from 1.11× to 0.99×, and T=512 from parity to 0.96×. Each warp in that kernel owns one token end-to-end and the early unconditional loads overlap subsequent work, so serializing the pos→cos/sin loads behind a branch costs more than the wasted L2 bandwidth saves. The asymmetry between the two kernels is deliberate and documented in the commit message.

#### Launch geometry: grid shape and CTA size (`5ab6c0fc4b`, `901bb03375`)

The `.cu` dispatches a second, reduced-grid kernel (one CTA per token, warps walking slots) above 1024 tokens. The initial port replicated that dispatch. Measuring the DSL's two grids against each other showed the DSL standard grid (one warp per `(token, slot)`) is faster at every size above the cutoff, so the reduced-grid kernel, its compile-key field, and `NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF` are deleted from the DSL module:

| T | reduced-grid µs | standard-grid µs |
|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 56.2 | 51.9 |
| 2048 | 108.6 | 105.4 |
| 4096 | 210.8 | 200.2 |
| 8192 | 410.1 | 399.7 |

Both grids are bit-exact against the `.cu`. The `.cu` keeps its own reduced-grid kernel; its per-warp slot loop is what its software prefetch (below) is written against, and the register cost of that pattern is why it needs the coarser grid.

CTA size is also measured, per kernel. The paged kernel moved from 256-thread to 128-thread CTAs (equal or faster at every size; T=64 4.68 → 4.44 µs, T=8192 440.4 → 437.9 µs). The full-cache kernel now carries its CTA size in the compile key and picks it per store dtype and launch size:

| T | bf16/128 | bf16/256 | fp8/128 | fp8/256 | `.cu` bf16 | `.cu` fp8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 2.32 | 2.45 | 2.54 | 2.40 | 2.87 | 2.73 |
| 512 | 5.53 | 5.64 | 5.03 | 4.50 | 5.70 | 5.05 |
| 1024 | 8.61 | 8.58 | 7.67 | 6.74 | 9.03 | – |
| 2048 | 15.11 | 15.33 | 15.76 | 16.99 | 17.20 | – |
| 4096 | 37.22 | 37.87 | 29.69 | 31.27 | 47.26 | 39.88 |

bf16 rows prefer 128-thread CTAs at every size. fp8 rows, half the bytes, prefer 256-thread CTAs while the working set is L2-resident (latency-bound) and 128-thread CTAs once the launch spills to DRAM, so the fp8 entry point switches at 2048 tokens. The same matrix is in the comment above the constants in the module.

#### SASS and occupancy, reduced-grid paged kernel

Measured before that variant was deleted; the numbers below explain the prefetch result that follows. Bench key: 64 Q heads padded to 128, q-norm + q-rope, bf16 KV, T at or above the reduced-grid cutoff.

| | `.cu` | DSL |
|---|---|---|
| instructions | 861 | 723 |
| registers/thread | 71 | 50 |
| resident CTAs/SM (warps) | 3 (24) | 5 (40) |
| LDG | 10 | 15 |
| SHFL | 16 | 7 |
| IMAD | 183 | 93 |

The DSL kernel is smaller and runs at higher occupancy, so the pre-guard deficit of 1-2% at T=2048/8192 came from memory-level parallelism rather than instruction count or occupancy. The rope-lane guard recovered it; the slot-loop prefetch below was the next attempt at the same asymmetry and was rejected.

#### Measured and rejected: slot-loop prefetch and buffer rotation

The `.cu`'s reduced-grid kernel software-prefetches the next slot's `uint4`s and rotates buffers inside the slot loop, and it calls `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()` once before the loop instead of once per iteration:

```cpp
if (warpId < slot_end) {
  int curr_slot = warpId; uint4 v0_curr, v1_curr;
  load_slot(curr_slot, v0_curr, v1_curr);          // prologue
  while (curr_slot < slot_end) {
    int const next_slot = curr_slot + warpsPerBlock;
    uint4 v0_next, v1_next;
    if (next_slot < slot_end) load_slot(next_slot, v0_next, v1_next); // prefetch
    processDeepseekV4Slot(v0_curr, ...);
    v0_curr = v0_next; v1_curr = v1_next;          // rotate
  }
}
```

Porting this to the DSL measured slower on every case it touches, with bit-exact outputs: quant_insert T=2048 108.6 → 111.2 µs, T=8192 410.0 → 431.1 µs, T=64 4.78 → 4.99 µs, kv_rope_insert 5.79 → 5.98 µs. The `.cu` fits this pattern in 71 registers because ptxas turns the buffer rotation into a register rename. In the DSL the rmem buffers are memrefs, so the rotation is an explicit per-slot word copy whose prefetched result must stay live across the full processing of the previous slot, and the register allocator grows the reduced-grid kernel from 50 to 110 registers per thread (`cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage`), cutting residency from 5 CTAs/SM (40 warps) to 2 (16 warps). At ~3.9 TB/s the kernel does not lack memory-level parallelism, so the prefetch trades occupancy it cannot spare for overlap it already has. The DSL slot loop stays serial. The reduced-grid kernel carrying that slot loop was later deleted outright (see the launch-geometry section); this result is recorded for anyone re-introducing a slot loop in the DSL.

#### Methodology

Each optimization was measured with an ablation harness on the H200 pod: apply one source edit to the module in place, bench in a restricted environment, restore the module, and compare against the unedited baseline. SASS came from `--keep-cubin` + `nvdisasm` dumps in a fresh cwd, because the DSL resolves the cubin output path from the process start directory. All numbers in the tables above were re-measured on the exact pushed artifact (md5-verified deployment), and the 227-test suite ran against that same artifact.

### End-to-end A/B on a serving cluster (H200, llm-d PD)

The branch was A/B'd against its exact base commit on a 2-node H200 prefill/decode deployment of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: 16 GPUs, TP1/DP8 per role, dspark speculative decoding with 3 draft tokens, bf16 weights (`deepseek_v4_fp8` quant), `fp8_ds_mla` packed KV records, nixl KV transfer, identical pinned nightly base image, router config, and node placement on both sides. Both vLLM builds came from the same upstream commit (`8b10bda57c`); the PR side is that commit plus only this branch (`901bb03375`). With `kv_cache_dtype=auto` on sm90 the serving path takes the packed-record branch, so this configuration runs `quant_insert` (the V4 584 B/token record; mxfp8 is capability-family-100 only), the entry point with the largest kernel-only wins above. Engine startup includes the CuTe DSL warmup (`enable_cutedsl_warmup=True`), so benchmarks ran against already-compiled kernels. Every run completed with zero errored requests.

- The kernel suite tests the DSL module directly; the AMD replay test keeps main's `torch.ops` path; the mono-numerics suites keep main's CDNA4-only gating (they exercise the extension op on ROCm); the compressor and PCP tests call/patch the dispatch functions.
- Local: `py_compile`, pinned-ruff (0.14.0) check + format, and the CI mypy wrapper (1.20.2) clean on the changed files; CUDA suites to run in CI.

Math is ported bit for bit: fp32 accumulation, bf16 double-round before the absmax, warp shuffle reduction order, UE8M0 exponent-field scales, both paged record layouts (V4 584 B/token, V4.1 mxfp8 528 B/token), the full-cache bf16/fp8 variants, and graph-replay-safe launches. Scalar min/max/abs/rsqrt use the DSL's `cute.arch`/`cute.math` ops rather than hand-rolled helpers, and compile to the same instructions the .cu's intrinsics compiled to, with NaN handling following the hardware ops as in the .cu.

**ROCm is preserved.** The `.cu` stays but is built only for HIP (`CMakeLists.txt`), with its four torch ops registered under `#ifdef USE_ROCM`, so CUDA builds no longer compile or ship the kernel and AMD behavior is unchanged. The six production call sites (deepseek_v4/v41 attention and dspark) import the four functions from a new dispatch module, `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_dispatch`, which routes ROCm to the extension op and everything else to the CuTe DSL module (imported lazily, failing closed with a named RuntimeError when nvidia-cutlass-dsl is missing).

The `kv`-only entry point also takes optional `kv_norm_weight`/`kv_norm_eps`; current call sites leave them unset, and the ROCm op does not take them (the dispatch raises `NotImplementedError` there instead).

Each fix below came from diffing the DSL-generated SASS against the `.cu` SASS.

#### 128-bit vectorized memory access (`668d0b3bbd`)

The initial port touched memory through per-element DSL tensor indexing, which lowered to 32-bit loads and stores. Reworking the layouts so each lane's 16 elements move as one folded `cute.copy` with a 128-bit copy atom gave the paged kernel LDG.128/STG.128 and took quant_insert T=8192 from 1070 to ~453 µs (~1.4 to ~3.5 TB/s). The kernel is bandwidth-limited after this change, matching the `.cu`.

#### bf16 encode/store tail as one inline-asm block (`668d0b3bbd`)

This change fixed full_cache_bf16 (T=4096: 82 → 37.8 µs). The full-cache Q path ends with eight `cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32` (F2FP) feeding two 128-bit stores. In the DSL-generated SASS the eight conversions issued back-to-back and both stores waited on the last F2FP with nothing left to overlap. The `.cu` does not have this tail because its store address comes from runtime division and modulo, a long integer dependency chain that interleaves with the conversions.

The fix is `_q_tail_store_bf16`, a single inline-asm PTX block that owns both the conversions and the address math, hand-interleaved so the two chains hide each other:

```ptx
{
    .reg .b32 t0, t1, w0..w7;  .reg .b64 d0, d1;
    shl.b32            t0, $3, 8;               // slot   -> word offset
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w0, $6, $5;
    cvt.u64.u32        d0, t0;
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w1, $8, $7;
    mad.wide.u32       d1, $2, {row_words}, d0;  // token*row_words + slot
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w2, $10, $9;
    shl.b32            t1, $4, 3;                // lane   -> word offset
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w3, $12, $11;
    cvt.u64.u32        d0, t1;
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w4, $14, $13;
    add.u64            d1, d1, d0;
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w5, $16, $15;
    shl.b64            d1, d1, 2;                // words  -> bytes
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w6, $18, $17;
    add.u64            d1, d1, $1;               // + tensor base
    cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32  w7, $20, $19;
    st.global.v4.b32   [d1],    {w0, w1, w2, w3};
    st.global.v4.b32   [d1+16], {w4, w5, w6, w7};
}
```

The tensor base comes from `q.iterator.to_llvm_ptr()` → `llvm.ptrtoint(T.i64())` and is bound with the `l` constraint. `row_words` is a per-compile-key constant (`HQ * 256`), baked into the asm string as an immediate rather than passed as a register operand. The block is marked `has_side_effects=True` for the stores. It is bit-exact against `cute.copy` + `_encode_words` on every suite case, because the DSL's `fp32x2_to_bf16x2` lowers to `cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32`.

The asm tail slows the paged kernel at large T. Routing the paged kernel's Q store through this block (measured, then rejected) took T=2048 from 120.3 to 126.4 µs (0.94×) and T=8192 from 452.8 to 469.9 µs (0.96×). At 3.5+ TB/s, issuing stores early matters more than hiding conversion latency, and `cute.copy`'s folded store address issues earlier than an address chain interleaved with the conversions. The paged kernel keeps `cute.copy`, and only the latency-bound full-cache kernel uses the asm tail.

#### Rope-lane-guarded cos/sin loads in the paged kernels (`3f5bb3ad31`)

This change closed the last sub-parity cases (quant_insert T=2048/8192, 0.98×/0.99× → 1.09×/1.10×). RoPE only touches the last `ROPE_DIM` of each 512-dim head, which is 4 of 32 lanes per warp (`dim_base >= NOPE_DIM`). The rope step in the DSL was already guarded by that condition, but the cos/sin loads were not. SASS of the paged kernel before the fix contains four unpredicated `LDG.E.128` per lane on all 32 lanes:

```
/*1ca0*/  LDG.E.128 R8,  desc[UR6][R28.64+0x80] ;
/*1cb0*/  LDG.128   R12, desc[UR6][R28.64] ;
/*1cc0*/  LDG.E.128 R16, desc[UR6][R28.64+0x90] ;
/*1cd0*/  LDG.E.128 R20, desc[UR6][R28.64+0x10] ;
```

That is 2 KB of L2-resident loads per warp per slot where 256 B suffice. `_load_cos_sin` also computes `half_base = (dim_base - NOPE_DIM) >> 1`, which is negative on the 28 non-rope lanes, so those lanes loaded from out-of-bounds addresses (the values were never consumed, which is why nothing failed). The `.cu` guards all of this behind `is_rope_lane`. Guarding the `pos_ids` fetch and `_load_cos_sin` call with the same `dim_base >= NOPE_DIM` condition the rope step already uses is semantically identical (`pos` and `cos_v`/`sin_v` have no other reader) and improved T=2048/8192 by ~10% and mid T by 4-8% (T=64 1.39×→1.55×, T=512 1.44×→1.50×), at a small cost in the decode-size case (T=1 1.32×→1.21×).

The same guard slows the full-cache kernel. Applying it to the full-cache kernel's two identical load sites (measured, then reverted) dropped T=128 from 1.19× to 1.04×, T=256 from 1.11× to 0.99×, and T=512 from parity to 0.96×. Each warp in that kernel owns one token end-to-end and the early unconditional loads overlap subsequent work, so serializing the pos→cos/sin loads behind a branch costs more than the wasted L2 bandwidth saves. The asymmetry between the two kernels is deliberate and documented in the commit message.

#### Launch geometry: grid shape and CTA size (`5ab6c0fc4b`, `901bb03375`)

The `.cu` dispatches a second, reduced-grid kernel (one CTA per token, warps walking slots) above 1024 tokens. The initial port replicated that dispatch. Measuring the DSL's two grids against each other showed the DSL standard grid (one warp per `(token, slot)`) is faster at every size above the cutoff, so the reduced-grid kernel, its compile-key field, and `NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF` are deleted from the DSL module:

Measured before that variant was deleted; the numbers below explain the prefetch result that follows. Bench key: 64 Q heads padded to 128, q-norm + q-rope, bf16 KV, T at or above the reduced-grid cutoff.

| | `.cu` | DSL |

| instructions | 861 | 723 |
| registers/thread | 71 | 50 |
| resident CTAs/SM (warps) | 3 (24) | 5 (40) |
| LDG | 10 | 15 |

The DSL kernel is smaller and runs at higher occupancy, so the pre-guard deficit of 1-2% at T=2048/8192 came from memory-level parallelism rather than instruction count or occupancy. The rope-lane guard recovered it; the slot-loop prefetch below was the next attempt at the same asymmetry and was rejected.

#### Measured and rejected: slot-loop prefetch and buffer rotation

The `.cu`'s reduced-grid kernel software-prefetches the next slot's `uint4`s and rotates buffers inside the slot loop, and it calls `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()` once before the loop instead of once per iteration:

```cpp
if (warpId < slot_end) {
  int curr_slot = warpId; uint4 v0_curr, v1_curr;
  load_slot(curr_slot, v0_curr, v1_curr);          // prologue
  while (curr_slot < slot_end) {
    int const next_slot = curr_slot + warpsPerBlock;
    uint4 v0_next, v1_next;
    if (next_slot < slot_end) load_slot(next_slot, v0_next, v1_next); // prefetch
    processDeepseekV4Slot(v0_curr, ...);
    v0_curr = v0_next; v1_curr = v1_next;          // rotate
  }
}
```

Porting this to the DSL measured slower on every case it touches, with bit-exact outputs: quant_insert T=2048 108.6 → 111.2 µs, T=8192 410.0 → 431.1 µs, T=64 4.78 → 4.99 µs, kv_rope_insert 5.79 → 5.98 µs. The `.cu` fits this pattern in 71 registers because ptxas turns the buffer rotation into a register rename. In the DSL the rmem buffers are memrefs, so the rotation is an explicit per-slot word copy whose prefetched result must stay live across the full processing of the previous slot, and the register allocator grows the reduced-grid kernel from 50 to 110 registers per thread (`cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage`), cutting residency from 5 CTAs/SM (40 warps) to 2 (16 warps). At ~3.9 TB/s the kernel does not lack memory-level parallelism, so the prefetch trades occupancy it cannot spare for overlap it already has. The DSL slot loop stays serial. The reduced-grid kernel carrying that slot loop was later deleted outright (see the launch-geometry section); this result is recorded for anyone re-introducing a slot loop in the DSL.

+"""Fused DeepseekV4-MLA Q-norm/RoPE + KV RoPE/quant/insert, CuTe DSL port.
+
+CUDA port of csrc/fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu (still built
+for ROCm; the _dispatch module routes between the two). One warp owns
+one (token, head_slot) pair, 32 lanes x 16 elements = the 512-wide head:
+
+  slot < num_heads_q                     -> live Q  (optional RMSNorm + RoPE,
+                                             zero-padded to q_head_padded)
+  num_heads_q <= slot < q_head_padded    -> pad Q   (zero fill)
+  slot == q_head_padded                  -> KV      (RoPE + UE8M0 FP8 quant +
+                                             paged-cache insert)
+
+RoPE is GPT-J interleaved-pair on dims [448, 512), all math fp32, cos_sin
+layout [max_pos, 64] = cos || sin. Q output optionally lands in FlashMLA's
+chunk-interleaved layout (32 chunks of [num_heads, 16]).
+
+Paged-cache record layout per block of bs tokens, selected by kv_mxfp8:
+  V4    (584 B/token): [0, bs*576) token data (448 fp8 + 128 fp16/bf16 each),
+         then [bs*576, bs*584) UE8M0 scales, 7 real + 1 pad per token.
+  V4.1  (528 B/token, kv_mxfp8): per-token inline records,
+         [i*528, i*528+512) fp8 data + [i*528+512, (i+1)*528) 16 UE8M0
+         scales, one per 32 dims; RoPE dims are quantized too.
+
+The full-cache variants write a contiguous 512-wide token row in the cache's
+own dtype (bf16, or per-tensor-scaled e4m3) with no Q padding.
+
+Bit-exactness notes carried over from the .cu: the KV branch rounds through
+the input dtype before the absmax, the warp reductions use the same shuffle
+order (fp addition is not associative), and ceil(log2(absmax/448)) is
+computed from the float's exponent field, which is exact for normal inputs.
+Scalar min/max/abs/rsqrt go through cute.arch/cute.math, which lower to the
+same hardware instructions as the .cu's fmaxf/fminf/fabsf/rsqrtf.
+
+Memory access matches the .cu's width too: every per-lane group moves as
+128-bit vector ops (the .cu's uint4 loads/stores and float4 cos/sin loads).
+Host-side views expose each lane's group as a statically-shaped trailing
+mode, and the kernels move them with CopyG2ROp/CopyR2GOp copy atoms, so a
+512-wide head is 2 loads + 2 stores per lane instead of 16 + 16 scalars.
+This is why the wrappers reject inputs the .cu could not have handled
+either: row strides and base pointers must be 16-byte aligned where the
+.cu's uint4/float4 accesses required it.

+    bf16x2_to_fp32x2,

+    fp32x4_to_fp8x4,
+)

+    VllmCuTeDSLJitKernel,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform

+HEAD_DIM = 512
+ROPE_DIM = 64
+NOPE_DIM = HEAD_DIM - ROPE_DIM
+HALF_ROPE = ROPE_DIM // 2
+ELEMS_PER_LANE = HEAD_DIM // 32
+BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE = ELEMS_PER_LANE // 2
+FP8_WORDS_PER_LANE = ELEMS_PER_LANE // 4
+FP8_MAX = 448.0
+
+V4_DATA_BYTES = NOPE_DIM + ROPE_DIM * 2
+V4_DATA_WORDS = V4_DATA_BYTES // 4
+V4_ROPE_WORD_BASE = NOPE_DIM // 4
+V4_SCALE_BYTES = NOPE_DIM // 64 + 1

+MXFP8_DATA_WORDS = MXFP8_DATA_BYTES // 4
+MXFP8_SCALE_BYTES = HEAD_DIM // 32
+MXFP8_BYTES_PER_TOKEN = MXFP8_DATA_BYTES + MXFP8_SCALE_BYTES
+
+BLOCK_SIZE = 128
+WARPS_PER_BLOCK = BLOCK_SIZE // 32
+# Full-cache CTA size, chosen per store dtype and launch size. Kernel-only
+# microseconds on H200 (16 q heads, CUDA-graph replay):
+#
+#   T     bf16/128  bf16/256  fp8/128  fp8/256  .cu bf16  .cu fp8
+#   128      2.32      2.45     2.54     2.40     2.87     2.73
+#   512      5.53      5.64     5.03     4.50     5.70     5.05
+#   1024     8.61      8.58     7.67     6.74     9.03      -
+#   2048    15.11     15.33    15.76    16.99    17.20      -
+#   4096    37.22     37.87    29.69    31.27    47.26    39.88
+#
+# bf16 rows prefer 128-thread CTAs at every size. fp8 rows, half the bytes,
+# prefer 256-thread CTAs while the working set still fits in L2 (latency
+# bound) and 128-thread CTAs once the launch spills to DRAM.
+FULL_CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE = 128
+FULL_CACHE_FP8_L2_BLOCK_SIZE = 256
+FULL_CACHE_FP8_L2_TOKENS = 2048
+
+_DUMMY_TENSORS: dict[tuple[Any, ...], torch.Tensor] = {}
+
+
+def _dummy_tensor(device: torch.device, dtype: torch.dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
+    key = (device, dtype)
+    tensor = _DUMMY_TENSORS.get(key)
+    if tensor is None:
+        tensor = torch.empty((1,), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        _DUMMY_TENSORS[key] = tensor
+    return tensor
+
+
+def _dummy_q_words(
+    device: torch.device, heads: int, interleaved: bool, group_words: int
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Stand-in for an unused per-lane word view. The head count is real so
+    # the JIT's static strides match the compiled specialization; a
+    # zero-head launch is floored at one head exactly like its warmup fake.
+    h = max(heads, 1)
+    key = (device, "qw", heads, interleaved, group_words)
+    tensor = _DUMMY_TENSORS.get(key)
+    if tensor is None:
+        if interleaved:
+            tensor = torch.empty(
+                (1, 32, h, group_words), dtype=torch.uint32, device=device
+            )
+        else:
+            tensor = torch.empty(
+                (1, h, 32, group_words), dtype=torch.uint32, device=device
+            )
+        _DUMMY_TENSORS[key] = tensor
+    return tensor
+
+
+def _cos_sin_word_view(cos_sin: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # (max_pos, 16, 4): one float4 row per cos/sin quarter.
+    return cos_sin.reshape(cos_sin.shape[0], ROPE_DIM // 4, 4)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _clamp_fp8(x: Float32) -> Float32:
+    return cute.arch.fmin(cute.arch.fmax(x, Float32(-FP8_MAX)), Float32(FP8_MAX))
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _warp_sum(val: Float32) -> Float32:
+    # Offsets descend 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 like the .cu's warpSum; fp addition is
+    # not associative, so the shuffle order is part of the numerical contract.
+    for s in cutlass.range_constexpr(5):
+        val = val + cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(val, 16 >> s)
+    return val
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _warp4_max_abs(val: Float32) -> Float32:
+    peer = cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(val, 1)
+    val = cute.arch.fmax(val, peer)
+    peer = cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(val, 2)
+    return cute.arch.fmax(val, peer)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _warp2_max_abs(val: Float32) -> Float32:
+    return cute.arch.fmax(val, cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(val, 1))
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _decode_words(
+    words: cute.Tensor, elems: cute.Tensor, input_fp16: Constexpr[bool]
+) -> None:
+    for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+        if cutlass.const_expr(input_fp16):
+            even, odd = _fp16x2_to_fp32x2(words[w])
+        else:
+            even, odd = bf16x2_to_fp32x2(words[w])
+        elems[2 * w] = even
+        elems[2 * w + 1] = odd
+
+
+@dsl_user_op
+def _q_tail_store_bf16(
+    q: cute.Tensor,
+    token: Int32,
+    slot: Int32,
+    lane: Int32,
+    elems: cute.Tensor,
+    row_words: int,
+    *,
+    loc=None,
+    ip=None,
+) -> Uint32:
+    """Q-path bf16 tail: encode this lane's 16 floats and store both 128-bit
+    halves in a single inline-asm block.
+
+    The eight ``cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32`` are F2FP ops; with cute.copy the store
+    address folds at trace time, so nothing overlaps the converts and they
+    bunch up at the warp tail. Interleaving the dependent store-address
+    chain among the converts gives ptxas the same latency-hiding structure
+    the CUDA kernel gets from its runtime-division address math. The
+    converts and stores are the same instructions cute.copy would emit
+    (verified bit-exact), just scheduled around the address math.
+
+    q has the (rows, heads, 32, 8) word layout from _q_word_views; the byte
+    address of (token, slot, lane, word 0) is
+    (token * row_words + slot * 256 + lane * 8) * 4, where row_words is the
+    token stride in words (HQ * 256). In ``cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 d, a, b`` a
+    lands in the upper 16 bits and b in the lower, so word w packs
+    elems[2w+1] high and elems[2w] low.
+    """
+    ptr = q.iterator.to_llvm_ptr(loc=loc, ip=ip)
+    addr = llvm.ptrtoint(T.i64(), ptr, loc=loc, ip=ip)
+    ins = [
+        addr,
+        token.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip),
+        slot.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip),
+        lane.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip),
+    ]
+    ins += [elems[i].ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip) for i in range(ELEMS_PER_LANE)]
+    asm = (
+        "{\n\t"
+        ".reg .b32 t0, t1, w0, w1, w2, w3, w4, w5, w6, w7;\n\t"
+        ".reg .b64 d0, d1;\n\t"
+        "shl.b32 t0, $3, 8;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 w0, $6, $5;\n\t"
+        "cvt.u64.u32 d0, t0;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 w1, $8, $7;\n\t"
+        f"mad.wide.u32 d1, $2, {row_words}, d0;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 w2, $10, $9;\n\t"
+        "shl.b32 t1, $4, 3;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 w3, $12, $11;\n\t"
+        "cvt.u64.u32 d0, t1;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 w4, $14, $13;\n\t"
+        "add.u64 d1, d1, d0;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 w5, $16, $15;\n\t"
+        "shl.b64 d1, d1, 2;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 w6, $18, $17;\n\t"
+        "add.u64 d1, d1, $1;\n\t"
+        "cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 w7, $20, $19;\n\t"
+        "st.global.v4.b32 [d1], {w0, w1, w2, w3};\n\t"
+        "st.global.v4.b32 [d1+16], {w4, w5, w6, w7};\n\t"
+        "mov.u32 $0, w0;\n\t"
+        "}\n"
+    )
+    out = llvm.inline_asm(
+        T.i32(),
+        ins,
+        asm,
+        "=r,l,r,r,r" + ",f" * ELEMS_PER_LANE,
+        has_side_effects=True,
+        is_align_stack=False,
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )
+    return Uint32(out)
+

+@dsl_user_op
+def _fp16x2_to_fp32x2(data: Uint32, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> tuple[Float32, Float32]:
+    out = llvm.inline_asm(
+        llvm.StructType.get_literal([T.f32(), T.f32()]),
+        [data.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip)],
+        "{ .reg .b16 lo, hi; mov.b32 {lo, hi}, $2; "
+        "cvt.f32.f16 $0, lo; cvt.f32.f16 $1, hi; }",
+        "=f,=f,r",
+        has_side_effects=False,
+        is_align_stack=False,
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )
+    return (
+        Float32(llvm.extractvalue(T.f32(), out, [0], loc=loc, ip=ip)),
+        Float32(llvm.extractvalue(T.f32(), out, [1], loc=loc, ip=ip)),
+    )
+
+
+@dsl_user_op
+def _fp32x2_to_fp16x2(a: Float32, b: Float32, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> Uint32:
+    out = llvm.inline_asm(
+        T.i32(),
+        [a.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip), b.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip)],
+        "cvt.rn.f16x2.f32 $0, $2, $1;",
+        "=r,f,f",
+        has_side_effects=False,
+        is_align_stack=False,
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )
+    return Uint32(out)

+@cute.jit
+def _encode_words(
+    elems: cute.Tensor, words: cute.Tensor, input_fp16: Constexpr[bool]
+) -> None:
+    for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+        if cutlass.const_expr(input_fp16):
+            words[w] = _fp32x2_to_fp16x2(elems[2 * w], elems[2 * w + 1])
+        else:
+            words[w] = fp32x2_to_bf16x2(elems[2 * w], elems[2 * w + 1])
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _round_to_fp16(elems: cute.Tensor) -> None:
+    for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(ELEMS_PER_LANE):
+        w = _fp32x2_to_fp16x2(elems[i], elems[i])
+        lo, _ = _fp16x2_to_fp32x2(w)
+        elems[i] = lo
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _round_to_bf16(elems: cute.Tensor) -> None:
+    # KV quant must read the bf16-rounded values the unfused norm-then-insert
+    # pipeline would have written and read back: two roundings, not one.
+    for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(ELEMS_PER_LANE):
+        w = fp32x2_to_bf16x2(elems[i], elems[i])
+        _, lo = bf16x2_to_fp32x2(w)
+        elems[i] = lo
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _apply_q_norm(elems: cute.Tensor, eps: Float32) -> None:
+    sum_sq = Float32(0.0)
+    for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(ELEMS_PER_LANE):
+        sum_sq = sum_sq + elems[i] * elems[i]
+    sum_sq = _warp_sum(sum_sq)
+    rcp = cute.math.rsqrt(sum_sq / Float32(HEAD_DIM) + eps, fastmath=True)
+    for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(ELEMS_PER_LANE):
+        elems[i] = elems[i] * rcp
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _apply_kv_norm(
+    elems: cute.Tensor, dim_base: Int32, eps: Float32, norm_w: cute.Tensor
+) -> None:
+    sum_sq = Float32(0.0)
+    for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(ELEMS_PER_LANE):
+        sum_sq = sum_sq + elems[i] * elems[i]
+    sum_sq = _warp_sum(sum_sq)
+    inv_rms = Float32(1.0) / cute.math.sqrt(sum_sq / Float32(HEAD_DIM) + eps)
+    for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+        even_w, odd_w = bf16x2_to_fp32x2(norm_w[dim_base // 2 + w])
+        elems[2 * w] = elems[2 * w] * inv_rms * even_w
+        elems[2 * w + 1] = elems[2 * w + 1] * inv_rms * odd_w
+    _round_to_bf16(elems)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _load_cos_sin(
+    cos_sin: cute.Tensor,
+    pos: Int64,
+    dim_base: Int32,
+    cs_atom: cute.CopyAtom,
+    cos_v: cute.Tensor,
+    sin_v: cute.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    # cos_sin is viewed (max_pos, 16, 4): rows 0..7 hold cos, 8..15 sin, one
+    # float4 per row. On rope lanes half_base is a multiple of 8, so this
+    # lane's 8 cos and 8 sin values are exactly two rows each — the .cu's
+    # four float4 loads. `& 7` is the identity on those lanes and parks every
+    # other lane on a valid stand-in row, so all 32 lanes can issue the loads
+    # up front — before the q/kv load and the RMSNorm reduction — instead of
+    # paying the latency inside the rope branch.
+    half_base = (dim_base - NOPE_DIM) >> 1
+    hb4 = (half_base >> 2) & Int32(7)
+    for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+        cute.copy(cs_atom, cos_sin[pos, Int32(hb4 + j), None], cos_v[j, None])
+        cute.copy(
+            cs_atom,
+            cos_sin[pos, Int32(HALF_ROPE // 4 + hb4 + j), None],
+            sin_v[j, None],
+        )
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _apply_rope(elems: cute.Tensor, cos_v: cute.Tensor, sin_v: cute.Tensor) -> None:
+    # cos_v/sin_v carry this lane's 8 cos and 8 sin values, preloaded by
+    # _load_cos_sin; only rope lanes call this.
+    for p in cutlass.range_constexpr(ELEMS_PER_LANE // 2):
+        c = cos_v[p // 4, p % 4]
+        s = sin_v[p // 4, p % 4]
+        x_even = elems[2 * p]
+        x_odd = elems[2 * p + 1]
+        elems[2 * p] = x_even * c - x_odd * s
+        elems[2 * p + 1] = x_even * s + x_odd * c
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _ue8m0_scale(absmax: Float32) -> tuple[Int32, Float32]:
+    # ceil(log2(absmax / FP8_MAX)) without libm: for normal y > 0 the biased
+    # exponent is exactly floor(log2(y)), so the ceil is that plus one iff the
+    # mantissa is nonzero. exp2 of an integer exponent is then an exact power
+    # of two via bitcast. absmax is floored at 1e-4 upstream, so y stays
+    # normal.
+    y = absmax / Float32(FP8_MAX)
+    bits = recast_val(y, Uint32)
+    exponent = Int32((bits >> 23) & 0xFF) - 127
+    if (bits & 0x7FFFFF) != Uint32(0):
+        exponent = exponent + 1
+    inv_scale = recast_val(Int32((127 - exponent) << 23), Float32)
+    return exponent, inv_scale
+
+
+def _paged_cache_views(
+    k_cache: torch.Tensor, cache_block_size: int, kv_mxfp8: bool
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Split a uint8 paged cache into its u32 data and u8 scale views.
+
+    Accepts [num_blocks, block_bytes] 2D or [num_blocks, bs, row_bytes] 3D
+    (rows must be packed: stride(1) == size(2)); the .cu addressed tokens at
+    fixed byte offsets within a block, so anything else was never a valid
+    input. Returns (data, scale):
+
+      V4:    data [B, bs, 144] u32 stride (S0//4, 144, 1),
+             scale [B, bs, 8] u8 stride (S0, 8, 1)    (tail after bs*576)
+      mxfp8: data [B, bs, 128] u32 stride (S0//4, 132, 1),
+             scale [B, bs, 16] u8 stride (S0, 528, 1) (inline per token)
+    """
+    row_bytes = MXFP8_BYTES_PER_TOKEN if kv_mxfp8 else V4_BYTES_PER_TOKEN
+    block_bytes = cache_block_size * row_bytes
+    if k_cache.dim() == 2:
+        flat = k_cache
+        if flat.stride(1) != 1:
+            raise ValueError("k_cache rows must be byte-contiguous (stride 1)")
+    elif k_cache.dim() == 3:
+        if k_cache.stride(2) != 1:
+            raise ValueError("k_cache rows must be byte-contiguous (stride 1)")
+        if k_cache.stride(1) != k_cache.shape[2]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "k_cache rows must be packed (stride(1) == size(2)); the "
+                "record layout is addressed at fixed offsets within a block"
+            )
+        flat = k_cache.view(k_cache.shape[0], -1)
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"k_cache must be 2D or 3D, got {k_cache.dim()}D")
+    if flat.shape[1] < block_bytes:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"k_cache row width {flat.shape[1]} is smaller than one "
+            f"{cache_block_size}-token block ({block_bytes} bytes)"
+        )
+    if flat.stride(0) % 16 != 0:
+        # The .cu's uint4 stores (and this port's 128-bit copies) require it.
+        raise ValueError("k_cache block stride must be 16-byte aligned")
+    num_blocks = flat.shape[0]
+    if kv_mxfp8:
+        records = flat[:, :block_bytes].view(
+            num_blocks, cache_block_size, MXFP8_BYTES_PER_TOKEN
+        )
+        data = records[:, :, :MXFP8_DATA_BYTES].view(torch.uint32)
+        scale = records[:, :, MXFP8_DATA_BYTES:]
+    else:
+        data = (
+            flat[:, : cache_block_size * V4_DATA_BYTES]
+            .view(num_blocks, cache_block_size, V4_DATA_BYTES)
+            .view(torch.uint32)
+        )
+        scale = flat[
+            :,
+            cache_block_size * V4_DATA_BYTES : cache_block_size * V4_BYTES_PER_TOKEN,
+        ].view(num_blocks, cache_block_size, V4_SCALE_BYTES)
+    return data, scale
+
+
+def _cache_word_views(
+    data: torch.Tensor, kv_mxfp8: bool
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Split a (blocks, bs, words) u32 cache-data view into the per-lane
+    group views the kernel copies through: 4-word groups for the fp8 stores
+    and 8-word groups for the V4 bf16 rope tail. Under mxfp8 the 8-word view
+    is a stand-in that no store ever targets."""
+    num_blocks, block_slots = data.shape[0], data.shape[1]
+    stride0 = data.stride(0)
+    if kv_mxfp8:
+        fp8 = data.as_strided(
+            (num_blocks, block_slots, MXFP8_DATA_WORDS // 4, 4),
+            (stride0, MXFP8_BYTES_PER_TOKEN // 4, 4, 1),
+        )
+        bf16 = data.as_strided(
+            (num_blocks, block_slots, MXFP8_DATA_WORDS // 8, 8),
+            (stride0, MXFP8_DATA_WORDS, 8, 1),
+        )
+    else:
+        fp8 = data.as_strided(
+            (num_blocks, block_slots, V4_DATA_WORDS // 4, 4),
+            (stride0, V4_DATA_WORDS, 4, 1),
+        )
+        bf16 = data.as_strided(
+            (num_blocks, block_slots, V4_DATA_WORDS // 8, 8),
+            (stride0, V4_DATA_WORDS, 8, 1),
+        )
+    return fp8, bf16
+
+
+def _q_word_views(t: torch.Tensor, heads: int, interleaved: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """View a [rows, heads, 512] bf16 tensor as u32 words grouped per lane:
+    (rows, heads, 32, 8), or (rows, 32, heads, 8) for the FlashMLA
+    chunk-interleaved layout. The trailing (8,) mode is one lane's group,
+    32 bytes at a 32-byte boundary."""
+    rows = t.shape[0]
+    words = t.view(torch.uint32)
+    if interleaved:
+        return words.as_strided((rows, 32, heads, 8), (heads * 256, heads * 8, 8, 1))
+    return words.reshape(rows, heads, 32, 8)
+
+
+def _kv_word_view(kv: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    words = kv.view(torch.uint32)
+    return words.as_strided((words.shape[0], 32, 8), (words.stride(0), 8, 1))
+
+
+def _full_cache_word_views(
+    cache_u32: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """(blocks, bs, 512-wide rows) u32 cache -> 8-word and 4-word group
+    views, each exactly covering the row. Only the one selected by the
+    store dtype is ever sliced."""
+    num_blocks, block_slots = cache_u32.shape[0], cache_u32.shape[1]
+    stride0, row = cache_u32.stride(0), cache_u32.stride(1)
+    row_words = cache_u32.shape[2]
+    bf16 = cache_u32.as_strided(
+        (num_blocks, block_slots, row_words // 8, 8), (stride0, row, 8, 1)
+    )
+    fp8 = cache_u32.as_strided(
+        (num_blocks, block_slots, row_words // 4, 4), (stride0, row, 4, 1)
+    )
+    return fp8, bf16
+
+
+def _check_common(
+    op_name: str,
+    kv: torch.Tensor,
+    slot_mapping: torch.Tensor,
+    position_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    allow_fp16: bool = False,
+) -> None:
+    if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{op_name}: the CuTe DSL port is CUDA-only; this platform has "
+            "no implementation"
+        )
+    if not kv.is_cuda:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: kv must be a CUDA tensor")
+    if kv.dtype != torch.bfloat16 and not (allow_fp16 and kv.dtype == torch.float16):
+        expected = "bfloat16 or float16" if allow_fp16 else "bfloat16"
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: kv must be {expected}, got {kv.dtype}")
+    if kv.dim() != 2 or kv.shape[1] != HEAD_DIM or kv.stride(1) != 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: kv must be [tokens, {HEAD_DIM}] row-major")
+    if kv.stride(0) % 8 != 0:
+        # 16 bytes: the .cu's uint4 loads require it, and so do this
+        # port's 128-bit vector loads.
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: kv row stride must be 16-byte aligned")
+    if kv.data_ptr() % 16 != 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: kv must be 16-byte aligned")
+    for name, tensor in (
+        ("slot_mapping", slot_mapping),
+        ("position_ids", position_ids),
+    ):
+        if (
+            tensor.dtype != torch.int64
+            or tensor.dim() != 1
+            or not tensor.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: {name} must be contiguous 1D int64")
+        if tensor.device != kv.device:
+            raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: {name} must be on the KV device")
+    if position_ids.shape[0] != kv.shape[0]:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: positions must match KV rows "
+            f"({position_ids.shape[0]} vs {kv.shape[0]})"
+        )
+    if slot_mapping.shape[0] > kv.shape[0]:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: slot_mapping must not exceed KV rows "
+            f"({slot_mapping.shape[0]} vs {kv.shape[0]})"
+        )
+    if (
+        cos_sin_cache.dtype != torch.float32
+        or cos_sin_cache.dim() != 2
+        or cos_sin_cache.shape[1] != ROPE_DIM
+        or not cos_sin_cache.is_contiguous()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: cos_sin_cache must be contiguous float32 [max_pos, {ROPE_DIM}]"
+        )
+    if cos_sin_cache.data_ptr() % 16 != 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: cos_sin_cache must be 16-byte aligned")
+    if cos_sin_cache.device != kv.device:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: cos_sin_cache must be on the KV device")
+
+
+def _check_scalar(
+    op_name: str, name: str, scale: torch.Tensor, device: torch.device
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if scale.dtype != torch.float32 or scale.numel() != 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: {name} must be one float32 scalar")
+    if scale.device != device:
+        raise ValueError(f"{op_name}: {name} must be on the KV device")
+    return scale.reshape(1)
+

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PagedCompileKey:
+    num_heads_q: int
+    q_head_padded: int
+    apply_q_norm: bool
+    apply_q_rope: bool
+    is_q_interleaved: bool
+    kv_mxfp8: bool
+    has_kv_norm: bool
+    input_fp16: bool
+    eps: float
+
+
+class _PagedInsertKernel(VllmCuTeDSLJitKernel[PagedCompileKey]):
+    """Paged-record variant: V4/V4.1 UE8M0 quantizing insert."""
+
+    CompileKey = PagedCompileKey
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def kernel(compile_key: PagedCompileKey) -> Any:
+        HQ = compile_key.num_heads_q
+        QP = compile_key.q_head_padded
+        APPLY_Q_NORM = compile_key.apply_q_norm
+        APPLY_Q_ROPE = compile_key.apply_q_rope
+        Q_INTERLEAVED = compile_key.is_q_interleaved
+        KV_MXFP8 = compile_key.kv_mxfp8
+        HAS_KV_NORM = compile_key.has_kv_norm
+        INPUT_FP16 = compile_key.input_fp16
+        EPS = Float32(compile_key.eps)
+        USE_PDL = current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()
+
+        @cute.jit
+        def process_slot(
+            token: Int32,
+            slot: Int32,
+            lane: Int32,
+            dim_base: Int32,
+            q_in: cute.Tensor,
+            q_out: cute.Tensor,
+            kv: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_fp8: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_bf16: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_scale: cute.Tensor,
+            slots: cute.Tensor,
+            pos_ids: cute.Tensor,
+            cos_sin: cute.Tensor,
+            norm_w: cute.Tensor,
+            load_atom: cute.CopyAtom,
+            store_atom: cute.CopyAtom,
+            cs_atom: cute.CopyAtom,
+            n_insert: Int32,
+            block_size: Int32,
+        ) -> None:
+            if slot == Int32(QP):
+                # KV slot: RoPE + quant + insert, only for the first
+                # n_insert rows (with DP padding, tail rows have no slot).
+                if token < n_insert:
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                        cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+                    cs_layout = cute.make_layout((2, 4), stride=(4, 1))
+                    cos_v = cute.make_rmem_tensor(cs_layout, Float32)
+                    sin_v = cute.make_rmem_tensor(cs_layout, Float32)
+                    # Only rope lanes (dim_base >= NOPE_DIM, 4 of 32) read
+                    # cos_v/sin_v; skip the 128-bit cos/sin loads elsewhere,
+                    # matching the .cu's is_rope_lane guard.
+                    if dim_base >= Int32(NOPE_DIM):
+                        pos = pos_ids[token]
+                        _load_cos_sin(cos_sin, pos, dim_base, cs_atom, cos_v, sin_v)
+                    elems = cute.make_rmem_tensor((ELEMS_PER_LANE,), Float32)
+                    words = cute.make_rmem_tensor((BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE,), Uint32)
+                    cute.copy(load_atom, kv[token, Int32(lane), None], words[None])
+                    _decode_words(words, elems, INPUT_FP16)
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(HAS_KV_NORM):
+                        _apply_kv_norm(elems, dim_base, EPS, norm_w)
+                    if dim_base >= Int32(NOPE_DIM):
+                        _apply_rope(elems, cos_v, sin_v)
+                    sid = slots[token]
+                    if sid >= Int64(0):
+                        block = sid // Int64(block_size)
+                        pib = sid % Int64(block_size)
+                        if cutlass.const_expr(INPUT_FP16):
+                            _round_to_fp16(elems)
+                        else:
+                            _round_to_bf16(elems)
+                        local_max = Float32(0.0)
+                        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(ELEMS_PER_LANE):
+                            local_max = cute.arch.fmax(
+                                local_max, cute.math.abs(elems[i])
+                            )
+                        if cutlass.const_expr(KV_MXFP8):
+                            absmax = cute.arch.fmax(
+                                _warp2_max_abs(local_max), Float32(1e-4)
+                            )
+                        else:
+                            absmax = cute.arch.fmax(
+                                _warp4_max_abs(local_max), Float32(1e-4)
+                            )
+                        exponent, inv_scale = _ue8m0_scale(absmax)
+                        if cutlass.const_expr(KV_MXFP8):
+                            store_fp8 = True
+                        else:
+                            store_fp8 = dim_base < Int32(NOPE_DIM)
+                        if store_fp8:
+                            packed = cute.make_rmem_tensor(
+                                (FP8_WORDS_PER_LANE,), Uint32
+                            )
+                            for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(FP8_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                                v0 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w] * inv_scale)
+                                v1 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 1] * inv_scale)
+                                v2 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 2] * inv_scale)
+                                v3 = _clamp_fp8(elems[4 * w + 3] * inv_scale)
+                                packed[w] = fp32x4_to_fp8x4(v0, v1, v2, v3)
+                            cute.copy(
+                                store_atom,
+                                packed[None],
+                                cache_fp8[block, pib, Int32(lane), None],
+                            )
+                            encoded = exponent + 127
+                            if encoded > 255:
+                                encoded = 255
+                            if encoded < 0:
+                                encoded = 0
+                            if cutlass.const_expr(KV_MXFP8):
+                                # One scale per 32 dims = one per lane pair.
+                                if (lane & 1) == 0:
+                                    cache_scale[block, pib, Int64(lane >> 1)] = Uint8(
+                                        encoded
+                                    )
+                            else:
+                                if (lane & 3) == 0:
+                                    cache_scale[block, pib, Int64(lane >> 2)] = Uint8(
+                                        encoded
+                                    )
+                                if lane == 0:
+                                    # Pad byte the reader expects at index 7.
+                                    cache_scale[
+                                        block, pib, Int64(V4_SCALE_BYTES - 1)
+                                    ] = Uint8(0)
+                        else:
+                            _encode_words(elems, words, INPUT_FP16)
+                            # The rope tail lands at words [8L-112, 8L-104)
+                            # of the token row = tile L-14 of the 8-word view.
+                            cute.copy(
+                                store_atom,
+                                words[None],
+                                cache_bf16[block, pib, Int32(lane - 14), None],
+                            )
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                        cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+            else:
+                # Q slot: pad slots only zero-fill; live slots decode,
+                # optionally norm and rope, then re-encode.
+                if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+                if slot < Int32(HQ):
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(APPLY_Q_ROPE):
+                        cs_layout = cute.make_layout((2, 4), stride=(4, 1))
+                        cos_v = cute.make_rmem_tensor(cs_layout, Float32)
+                        sin_v = cute.make_rmem_tensor(cs_layout, Float32)
+                        # Same rope-lane guard as the KV slot above.
+                        if dim_base >= Int32(NOPE_DIM):
+                            pos = pos_ids[token]
+                            _load_cos_sin(cos_sin, pos, dim_base, cs_atom, cos_v, sin_v)
+                    elems = cute.make_rmem_tensor((ELEMS_PER_LANE,), Float32)
+                    words = cute.make_rmem_tensor((BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE,), Uint32)
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(Q_INTERLEAVED):
+                        cute.copy(
+                            load_atom,
+                            q_in[token, Int32(lane), slot, None],
+                            words[None],
+                        )
+                    else:
+                        cute.copy(
+                            load_atom,
+                            q_in[token, slot, Int32(lane), None],
+                            words[None],
+                        )
+                    _decode_words(words, elems, INPUT_FP16)
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(APPLY_Q_NORM):
+                        _apply_q_norm(elems, EPS)
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(APPLY_Q_ROPE):  # noqa: SIM102

+                    if cutlass.const_expr(Q_INTERLEAVED):
+                        cute.copy(
+                            store_atom,
+                            words[None],
+                            q_out[token, Int32(lane), slot, None],
+                        )
+                    else:
+                        cute.copy(
+                            store_atom,
+                            words[None],
+                            q_out[token, slot, Int32(lane), None],
+                        )
+                else:
+                    # FlashMLA reads the pad slots; bf16 +0.0 is 0x0000.
+                    words = cute.make_rmem_tensor((BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE,), Uint32)
+                    for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(BF16_WORDS_PER_LANE):
+                        words[w] = Uint32(0)
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(Q_INTERLEAVED):
+                        cute.copy(
+                            store_atom,
+                            words[None],
+                            q_out[token, Int32(lane), slot, None],
+                        )
+                    else:
+                        cute.copy(
+                            store_atom,
+                            words[None],
+                            q_out[token, slot, Int32(lane), None],
+                        )
+                if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+                    cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+
+        @cute.kernel
+        def device_kernel(
+            q_in: cute.Tensor,
+            q_out: cute.Tensor,
+            kv: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_fp8: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_bf16: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_scale: cute.Tensor,
+            slots: cute.Tensor,
+            pos_ids: cute.Tensor,
+            cos_sin: cute.Tensor,
+            norm_w: cute.Tensor,
+            load_atom: cute.CopyAtom,
+            store_atom: cute.CopyAtom,
+            cs_atom: cute.CopyAtom,
+            n_full: Int32,
+            n_insert: Int32,
+            block_size: Int32,
+        ):
+            bidx, _, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+            warp = cute.arch.warp_idx()
+            lane = cute.arch.lane_idx()
+            gw = bidx * WARPS_PER_BLOCK + warp
+            token = gw // Int32(QP + 1)
+            slot = gw % Int32(QP + 1)
+            dim_base = lane * ELEMS_PER_LANE
+            if token < n_full:
+                process_slot(
+                    token,
+                    slot,
+                    lane,
+                    dim_base,
+                    q_in,
+                    q_out,
+                    kv,
+                    cache_fp8,
+                    cache_bf16,
+                    cache_scale,
+                    slots,
+                    pos_ids,
+                    cos_sin,
+                    norm_w,
+                    load_atom,
+                    store_atom,
+                    cs_atom,
+                    n_insert,
+                    block_size,
+                )
+
+        @cute.jit
+        def host_entrypoint(
+            q_in: cute.Tensor,
+            q_out: cute.Tensor,
+            kv: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_fp8: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_bf16: cute.Tensor,
+            cache_scale: cute.Tensor,
+            slots: cute.Tensor,
+            pos_ids: cute.Tensor,
+            cos_sin: cute.Tensor,
+            norm_w: cute.Tensor,
+            stream: CUstream,
+        ):
+            load_atom = cute.make_copy_atom(
+                cute.nvgpu.CopyG2ROp(), Uint32, num_bits_per_copy=128
+            )
+            store_atom = cute.make_copy_atom(
+                cute.nvgpu.CopyR2GOp(), Uint32, num_bits_per_copy=128
+            )
+            cs_atom = cute.make_copy_atom(
+                cute.nvgpu.CopyG2ROp(), Float32, num_bits_per_copy=128
+            )
+            n = kv.shape[0]
+            ni = slots.shape[0]
+            bs = cache_fp8.shape[1]
+            device_kernel(
+                q_in,
+                q_out,
+                kv,
+                cache_fp8,
+                cache_bf16,
+                cache_scale,
+                slots,
+                pos_ids,
+                cos_sin,
+                norm_w,
+                load_atom,
+                store_atom,
+                cs_atom,
+                n,
+                ni,
+                bs,
+            ).launch(
+                grid=(
+                    (n * (QP + 1) + WARPS_PER_BLOCK - 1) // WARPS_PER_BLOCK,
+                    1,
+                    1,
+                ),
+                block=(BLOCK_SIZE, 1, 1),
+                stream=stream,
+                use_pdl=USE_PDL,
+            )
+
+        return host_entrypoint

+    def dispatch(  # type: ignore[override]
+        self,
+        **compile_key_fields: Any,
+    ) -> PagedCompileKey:
+        return self.CompileKey(**compile_key_fields)
+
+    def get_warmup_keys(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> list[PagedCompileKey]:
+        return []
+
+    def warmup_inputs(self, compile_key: PagedCompileKey) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
+        # Head counts are compile-key constants, so the q views' strides are
+        # static; a stand-in for an unused q view is floored at one head.
+        hq = max(compile_key.num_heads_q, 1)
+        qp = max(compile_key.q_head_padded, 1)
+        n = cute.sym_int()
+        i = cute.sym_int()
+        p = cute.sym_int()
+        b = cute.sym_int()
+        bs = cute.sym_int()
+        qt = cute.sym_int()
+        qot = cute.sym_int()
+        wt = cute.sym_int()
+        data_stride0 = cute.sym_int64(divisibility=4)
+        scale_stride0 = cute.sym_int64(divisibility=1)
